title: Texas tours and a killing outside Orange
summary: He describes train tours through Texas and a frightening night in Orange where the truck driver was shot and the band still had to play for cowboys.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Oh yeah, I've been all over the state of Ohio, Pennsylvania. I made good money just with my little combo. When I come back to New Orleans, well that's where I got famous then, you see, after I got here and everybody knew that I was back in town. I got jobs. We used to go all through Texas. We had a porter used to catch us on the train, see. They used to take the whole band nine minutes for 35 hours. And you'd ride the train. Used to get jobs all in Galveston, Houston, Orange, Texas. I never want to go back there no more. What happened there? We was in a truck, advertising, you know like you go around Ballyhorn, and they had some fellas following us. And so I said, these fellas following us, like the band might give us a job or something. So when we got on the outskirts, we didn't have no house like Suesbury, you know, from New Orleans. They pull up and asked the fellas, he said, stop the truck. So he stopped the truck and he said, get out. So he said, you got your gun? He said, no, I don't have my gun. He said, lie me a chance. And they shot him in the road and asked us which one of us could drive the truck. I told them I could drive the truck. Wait a minute, they shot who? Shot the driver. I don't know, it must have been a whiskey deal or some kind of deal. I was so scared, I never do want to go to Orange, Texas no more. They shot the driver? Yeah, killed him and told us to leave him in the road. I said leave him in the road.
I said, y'all go ahead and play your music.
And that night we played with them guys, I said, I said, I said, I said, I said, I said, I don't want to eat an orange no more. You guys come up there with horses, you know, on horses, in the hall.

I was riding them cowboys, you know how them cowboys, they rough. I said I don't want to eat orange no more. I don't eat orange no more. Don't hear nothing about orange touches. They had us playing Casey Jones and the Black Cat and everything. I played it. I was scared too, I'm telling you. I said when I get out there I'll lie, I ain't coming back.
You've got to believe it. That road's a tough thing, I wonder you don't go on that road.

No indeed I give the road up, I give it up. Yeah, I don't know, I'm going to try to get back on Boyle Street if I get a break. If I get a break I'm going to try to get out there. Rick and I tried to get me to play with him at the Mardi Gras. But see I was working out there, you see at Bramson, I couldn't stay at them hours a night, you know what I mean?
